reason: In peat mosses this means 'the hyaline cells have no fibrils' (wall thickenings), so it says a part is absent. Neither PO nor FLOPO has a class for these fibrils, and the bearer is a cell rather than the stem or leaf it was attached to.
A moss capsule annulus that is revoluble rolls outward and comes away from the capsule mouth. The nearest existing quality is 'revolute' (rolled backwards). The bearer, annulus, has no PO class.
Shreddy bark comes off in strips or shreds. The definition of exfoliating already covers bark peeling off in strips.
This is a growth-season or ecological group (often standing in for C4 grasses), not a quality of a plant part.

label: tetradynamous
definition: A structural quality inhering in an androecium by virtue of its consisting of six stamens, four long and two short.
reason: A standard term for the stamens of the cabbage family, with no existing term. It sits beside FLOPO:0991167 didynamous, under the same parent. Botany-specific.
The seed coat forms a network whose meshes are long and set in lines. Reticulate captures the network; the long, lined-up meshes are lost.
This is absence of pores in the hyaline cells of peat mosses. The previous review rejected 'pore' as too generic, and there is no PO class for these pores. Same case as 'fibrilless'.
'Sub-' means 'nearly', so this is 'nearly tubular': the approximate-value pattern applied to PATO tubular.
'Nearly foliaceous'. The previous review mapped foliaceous to PATO leaf-like, so this is the approximate-value pattern on leaf-like. 'subf oliaceous' is the same word with a transcription break.

label: tooth-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being small, triangular and pointed, like a tooth of a toothed margin.
reason: Used the same way for reduced staminodes, lobes and petals. 'Dentated' (PATO_0001205) means bearing teeth, not shaped like one. Modelled on bract-like and scale-like.
Bracted means bearing bracts. Same rule as 'bracteate' (C205).

label: semisagittate
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being like one half of an arrowhead, with a single acute basal lobe directed backwards on one side.
reason: A standard term for lopsided stipules. Arrow-shaped (PATO_0001881) needs two basal lobes, so it is not a kind of sagittate.
A multicipital caudex or rhizome has many heads (crowns), meaning it branches near the top. Branched is the existing quality.
A count of parts: one vein (vascular bundle, PO_0005020), handled like '5-nerved'.

target: new: timing relative to another part
reason: It means the leaves appear after the flowers (or the flowers come when the plant has no leaves). That is a relation in time between two parts, said of the leaf, the inflorescence or the whole plant. The current patterns cover no time order, and there is no PATO parent for a single term.
French 'subnul' means reduced to almost nothing (pédicelle subnul = pedicel nearly absent). Same reading as the earlier rule obsolete → vestigial.
French 'cannelé' means fluted, with lengthwise grooves. Same rule as 'fluted' (C197).
Two shape values written as one word, 'oblong-obovate'. This is handled like 'linear-lanceolate' (the in-between pattern), not as a new term.
Rosetted means forming a rosette. Rosulate already has the synonyms rosette-forming and 'in a rosette'.
Two shape values joined into one word. Handled by the in-between pattern, not a new term.
A half-cylinder is flat on one side and convex on the other. That is the definition of plano-convex, which is already used for petioles.
Epedunculate means without a peduncle. Built like 'ebracteate' (C206).

label: trisyncolpate
definition: A structural quality inhering in a pollen grain by virtue of its having three furrow-like apertures (colpi) that meet and fuse at the poles.
reason: A standard term for a kind of pollen opening, with no PATO or FLOPO term. Same parent as other botany-specific structure terms.

target: new: both of two values (elongated PATO_0001154 and rhomboid PATO_0001938)
reason: Two values joined into one word. Here both apply at once (a stretched rhomboid), not a range between them, so the in-between pattern does not fit.
The previous review mapped 'nodose' to PATO knobbled (C331). 'Non-nodose' (French 'non noueuses') negates it.
Thinned margins and wall thinnings ('amincies') are thinner than the rest of the part.
French 'racine pivotante' means taproot. That is a part, and PO has it as primary root (exact synonym 'tap root').

label: mitriform
definition: A concave 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a mitre: a cone-shaped cap covering an apex, not split down one side.
reason: A standard term for moss calyptras and eucalypt bud caps. It contrasts with FLOPO:0991119 cucullate (hood-shaped) and has the same parent.
Prophyllate means bearing a prophyll (the first leaf of a side shoot), like 'bracteate'.
'Nearly kidney-shaped': the approximate-value pattern applied to PATO reniform, as for 'suborbicular'.
